title: Audit of the Mandarin backend excitation, boundaries, formants and level
hypothesis: The Mandarin backend is spectrally self-consistent: (a) less than 1e-3 of the energy lies above 0.45*sr at f0 up to 880 Hz, (b) sibilants /s sh x/ put more relative energy in 2-8 kHz than /f/ or vowels, (c) envelope jumps at phoneme boundaries do not exceed the largest within-phoneme envelope jump, (d) formant trajectories inside diphthongs move smoothly (frame-to-frame spectral flux below a hard-spliced control), and (e) the same nucleus rendered in different consonant contexts stays within 3 dB RMS.

notes: Completed on synthetic signals only; no listening test. Criteria (b) and (c) fail and are kept as failures. The audit found a real defect (noise mask was a bump at the lower band edge) whose fix introduced a second defect (10% of /s/ energy above 0.45*sr) that the same audit caught on the next pass.

errata: E1: the formant peak tracker is unreliable (ou naive max step 1734 Hz is a set-selection artefact; the nearest-frequency matcher reports the same value). The primary smoothness criterion moved to spectral flux; both tracker outputs are kept in audit.json.formant_steps.

E2: criterion (b) as pre-registered is invalid for a 4-10 kHz /s/; it passes in the pre_band_fix state only because the broken mask squeezed /s/ into 2-4 kHz. Judged FAIL on the final state and left as a failure.
E3: the band-pass fix regressed aliasing to 1.05e-1 above 0.45*sr (/s/ fall reached 13.5 kHz). Fixed by clamping the fall endpoint to 0.45*sample_rate; verified 2.12e-4.

E4: criterion (c) fails for ba/ka/sa while the sample-level click ratio stays <=1.08, i.e. the 5 ms frame RMS metric cannot separate a fast physical onset from a discontinuity. The criterion is left failing rather than redefined after the fact.
E5: README assembled after the three runs; the criteria text itself was written into metadata.json before the first run.
